publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Dielectric Materials: a Review
abstract: Dissolved gas analysis, together with furfuraldehyde results, can be used for transformer condition monitoring. The practical usefulness of DGA as an aid to decision making when faults are developing or occurring is generally recognised. The increase of furfural content of the oil can be related to transformer ageing and may give valuable information in cases where the replacement of an asset is being considered. Monitoring the condition of the oil in oil-filled electrical equipment, followed where necessary by remedial can extend the life of the equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Space charge-what it is, how it is measured and why measure it?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Dielectric Materials: a Review
abstract: The problem of how to measure actual charge distributions, and in particular space charge distributions, in cables and other insulated systems is considered. Two techniques have been developed. Both make use of applying a force pulse to the sample which disturbs the equilibrium charge distribution and hence generates a change in the plate charge which can be detected and amplified. Examples of experimental determination of charge distributions in polymeric samples, and the analyses of these in terms of charge densities and mobilities, are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Surface analysis applied to reinforced composites
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Dielectric Materials: a Review
abstract: Glass fibre reinforced polymer resin laminates are used as circuit boards in electronic equipment. The adhesion of fibres to polymeric resins is essential to good performance. The mechanisms of adhesion involving silane coupling agents are not straightforward because of the complexity of the deposit and the fact that a simple coupling model cannot account far the observations. In order to study these inconsistencies surface analytical techniques have been applied to model surfaces and to the fracture surfaces of fibre composites to identify the nature of the silane deposit and its interaction with the glass substrate and the resin matrix.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Structural analysis of materials by X-ray diffraction
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Dielectric Materials: a Review
abstract: X-ray diffraction is an important and useful technique in solid state chemistry and has been used since the beginning of this century in the characterisation of crystalline materials. The examples described here give some idea of the wide spectrum of applications of diffraction techniques, and in particular the measurement of properties that could affect the performance of dielectrics. Other applications include determination of crystal structure, stress measurements and quantitative analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ultrasonic NDT for defects/degradation in insulation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Dielectric Materials: a Review
abstract: The partial discharge test is the major tool at the disposal of the engineer to determine the integrity of a sample of insulation on production and its probable in-service performance. The test, when properly interpreted, yields information about the size of the discharge, but gives no indication as to the nature, position or geometry of the source. All of these parameters may affect the in-service performance of a sample. We have employed two ultrasound techniques which may be used in conjunction with the discharge test to give more information about the discharge source. The use of acoustic emission is similar to the partial discharge test in that a single reading is provided by the whole sample for each test. The result of the test varies, however, with the position of the acoustic transducer. Acoustic emission may thus be used to gain information about the position of the discharge source, and must be performed while the sample is 'live'. Further investigation, via the use of active ultrasound, of an area of interest may indicate the size of the discharge source. Interpretation of the signals produced by both ultrasound techniques yields information about the nature of the discharge source. Examples of flaw detection in commercially produced samples are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermal analysis techniques in the power industry
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Dielectric Materials: a Review
abstract: Thermal analysis techniques such as Differential Scanning Calorimetry and Thermogravimetric Analysis have a wide range of applications in the study of polymeric insulators used in power engineering. They made be used to characterise the thermal stability, degradation mechanisms and thermal history of materials. In forensic studies, they often allow the identification of the base material and the type and concentration of fillers used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of microscopy to dielectric mouldings
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Dielectric Materials: a Review
abstract: As submarine cable systems are designed for high reliability, manufacturing processes and screening techniques have been developed to a very high standard to eliminate defects and inhomogeneities detrimental to short and long term performance. This has been achieved by an understanding of the factors giving rise to electrical weaknesses and thereby controlling moulding processes accordingly. This presentation describes the results of a programme of work aimed at understanding DC breakdown and ageing behaviour of DC insulation in order to achieve high reliability at minimised cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
